evidence.description: The reciprocal of investmentPerSecond is passed through max and used directly as the repeating timer interval.

candidates.explanation: When investmentPerSecond is zero, its reciprocal is infinity. Taking max with 1 does not make that value finite, so an infinite interval reaches the timer scheduling API. The calculation has no handling for a zero rate.
candidates.title: Timer interval calculation does not handle a zero investment rate

evidence.description: The public method accepts an arbitrary Date and directly converts the calculated floating-point projection to Int.

candidates.explanation: Swift's floating-point-to-Int initializer traps when its input is non-finite or outside the representable Int range. The date difference and investment arithmetic are not checked before conversion, so extreme or non-finite dates, or sufficiently large calculated totals, can cause this public method to terminate execution rather than return a value.
candidates.title: Unchecked floating-point conversion can trap
